# Repository custom instructions

These instructions apply to work in this repository and reflect the owner's Settings preferences.

- Keep READMEs simple, concise and easy to scan. Use helpful emojis, a clear project description, key features and quick-start instructions.
- Preserve important setup steps, authorization requirements and known limitations. Move lengthy details into linked guides.
- Give every file and folder a short, distinct, descriptive label with an appropriate emoji. Use the linked repository label guide without renaming functional paths or modifying preserved originals.
- For GitHub file/folder rows, use distinct, meaningful commit messages rather than repeating a generic message. These rows display commit history, not separate descriptions. Make commits around actual coherent changes; do not create artificial history to label rows.
- Do not list folder contents in folder descriptions.
- Do not list file contents in file descriptions.
- Keep the GitHub About description concise and informative.
- Preserve application behavior, licenses and file contents when making presentation changes. Ask before rewriting published Git history.
